title: The Cut That Cannot Be Undone

scenes.tts: A cell must give each daughter one copy of every chromosome. Each chromosome is two sister copies, held together by a ring called cohesin. Each sister has a kinetochore, the machine that grips the spindle fibres. Fibres from opposite poles pull on the sisters. So what lets go, and why can the cell never take it back?
scenes.visual: Cell with two poles and three chromosomes; each is two sister bars held by a closed ring; fibres pull outward; a question mark lands on the ring.
scenes.narration: A cell must give each daughter one copy of every chromosome. Each chromosome is two sister copies, held together by a ring called cohesin. Each sister has a kinetochore, the machine that grips the spindle fibres. Fibres from opposite poles pull on the sisters. So what lets go, and why can the cell never take it back?

scenes.tts: First the cell checks its attachments. The right outcome is biorientation. The two sister kinetochores attach to opposite poles. That puts the sisters under tension, because the poles pull against the cohesin. Tension stabilizes the right attachments. A kinetochore that is still unattached sends a signal. That signal holds back the anaphase-promoting complex, with its coactivator C D C twenty. When every kinetochore is attached, the signal stops.

That signal holds back the anaphase-promoting complex, with its coactivator Cdc20. When every kinetochore is attached, the signal stops.
scenes.visual: One chromosome has a free kinetochore that sends a red signal to a blocked APC/C chip; the fibre then attaches, the signal stops and the block lifts.
scenes.narration: First the cell checks its attachments. The right outcome is biorientation. The two sister kinetochores attach to opposite poles. That puts the sisters under tension, because the poles pull against the cohesin. Tension stabilizes the right attachments. A kinetochore that is still unattached sends a signal. That signal holds back the anaphase-promoting complex, with its coactivator Cdc20. When every kinetochore is attached, the signal stops.

scenes.tts: Now the anaphase-promoting complex is released. It tags proteins with ubiquitin, which sends them to the proteasome. One target is securin. Securin binds an enzyme called separase and keeps it inactive. The tagged securin is destroyed, and in vertebrates so is cyclin B, which lifts a second brake. Nothing holds separase back now. Separase is free.
scenes.visual: APC/C tags securin with Ub badges; securin leaves the dimmed separase, goes to the proteasome and vanishes; cyclin B loss lifts a second brake in vertebrates; separase lights up.
scenes.narration: Now the anaphase-promoting complex is released. It tags proteins with ubiquitin, which sends them to the proteasome. One target is securin. Securin binds an enzyme called separase and keeps it inactive. The tagged securin is destroyed, and in vertebrates so is cyclin B, which lifts a second brake. Nothing holds separase back now. Separase is free.

scenes.tts: Separase is a protease. It cuts S C C one, one subunit of the cohesin ring, and the ring opens. A cut protein cannot be rejoined. So the sisters are free to part. In budding yeast cells held at metaphase, cutting S C C one was enough to separate the sisters.

scenes.visual: Large chromosome; separase docks on the Scc1 segment of the ring and cuts it; a crossed-out rejoin arrow marks the cut; the sisters part; a yeast label appears.
scenes.narration: Separase is a protease. It cuts Scc1, one subunit of the cohesin ring, and the ring opens. A cut protein cannot be rejoined. So the sisters are free to part. In budding yeast cells held at metaphase, cutting Scc1 was enough to separate the sisters.

scenes.tts: Anaphase has two movements. Anaphase A moves each chromosome toward its pole, as the fibres shorten. Anaphase B separates the poles themselves. Take an illustrative movie. The poles start twelve micrometres apart and end sixteen. Each kinetochore moves from five point five to one point five micrometres from its pole, in four minutes. The sisters separate at three micrometres per minute. That is twice anaphase A, plus anaphase B.

scenes.tts: So anaphase is a chain with one way through. Every kinetochore is attached. Securin is destroyed. Separase cuts S C C one. Then the chromosomes and the poles move apart. Keep this rule. A cut protein cannot be rejoined, so anaphase cannot be reversed.
